suggestions.title: Tomorrow morning: step on the scale — three mornings missed, and the two 160s are still an open question

rationale.science: One morning read is noise around a slow trend — for you the day-to-day noise is about ±1.5 lb. After a sudden drop, the only thing that tells water from fat is the next few clean reads; without them the trend just sits and the rate estimate gets wider, not wronger.
rationale.data: Last read Thursday 9/10 at 160.0 — the second 160 in a row, both damped by the app as spikes. No read Friday, Saturday, or today; the app wrote 'read missed' on each open. Its rate range widened from 0.46 lb/wk to 0.19–0.73. Monday's weekly row — the 162 milestone — is built tomorrow on a three-day gap.
rationale.relationship: The app holds low reads back until clean ones confirm them. One read tomorrow settles it: 161.5 or under and the 160s were a real catch-down (161 becomes the next stop); 162 or over and they were water and nothing is lost. Either answer also stops your maintenance estimate drifting upward on two unconfirmed mornings.

suggestions.predict: A morning read on file for 9/14 or 9/15 → hit. Sub-reads, not graded: ≤161.5 → the app's trend goes under 161.7 within two reads and I call the catch-down real; ≥162.0 → trend holds 161.7–162.0 and the 160s were water. No read by Wednesday's run → miss.

suggestions.title: Rear delts: four upper days skipped in a row — pick one: the Prime machine, magnets for the cable, or retire it

rationale.science: A muscle left untrained for three to four weeks starts giving back size and strength (Bosquet 2013; Mujika & Padilla 2000). Rear delts are small, so the body-composition cost is small — but on a cut every slot on the sheet should either get its hard sets or come off (Schoenfeld 2017: ~10 hard sets a week per muscle you want to keep).
rationale.data: Rear-delt fly skipped 8/20, 9/03, 9/06 and 9/10 — every upper day since it was last done on 8/16 at 20 × 10, 10, 8. Your queue already holds the Prime rear-delt switch; the app flagged the cable's 12.5% plate jump on 9/03. Not in retirements.
rationale.relationship: The plate jump is the likely reason the lift stalled at 20 and became the easy one to skip. Any of the three answers fixes the sheet; a fifth skip leaves a dead slot on every upper day. This is your decision — I'm asking for it, not making it.

suggestions.predict: Next upper day on file: rear delts logged on any machine at any load, or the lift appears in retirements → hit. A fifth skip with no retirement → miss, and I stop raising it.

suggestions.title: Fly: open at one to two reps in reserve — Thursday's first set was rated zero, and both sets dropped

rationale.science: On a deficit the goal is to defend the load with sets ending one to three reps short of failure (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024; Grgic 2021). Opening at true failure costs the later sets and gives a worse read of your strength, not a better one.
rationale.data: Fly at 90: last Sunday 12, 11 with the opener at 2 in reserve; Thursday 11, 10 with both sets rated 0. It was the only lift on Thursday's sheet that fell on every set — press, pulldown, laterals, rows and triceps all held or gained.
rationale.relationship: A zero-rated opener is exactly what froze abs and rows in August. You approved 'open at 1–2, not 0' on 8/9 and both holds released. Fly is the one lift where it slipped; open it at two in reserve and I expect 12 back on set one.

suggestions.predict: Next upper day: fly opener logged at 1–2 RIR and first set ≥12 at 90 → hit. Opener rated 0 again → miss regardless of reps. First set 11 at 1–2 RIR → hit on the ask, and I note the load, not the effort, as the question.
